name: New Zealand evidence-based ICT supplier-risk controls

attribution.legal_posture: General procurement guidance omits DPRK IT-worker discussion; it supplies procurement context rather than an allegation, incident, supplier finding, exclusion decision or adjudicated violation.

caveats: Apply documented supplier risk and proportional controls; nationality, language, location, and remote-work status require corroboration before exclusion.
Supplier or personnel data gathered during due diligence stays unpublished.
Guidance, sanctions, procurement, and coordination material supplies context rather than evidence of a named incident or adjudicated violation.
This is general procurement guidance. It supplies procurement context, with supplier allegations and nationality-based exclusion requiring separate rules or findings.
The public-sector procurement guidance addresses general procurement; a DPRK-specific advisory or incident response requires a separate source.
The dataset retains source-bounded context while excluding people, personas, accounts, entities, images, identifiers, victim or private data, payment data, wallets, and raw indicators.
Fraud or DPRK attribution requires corroboration beyond any single nationality, language, accent, location, camera behavior, remote-work preference, technical tool or other weak signal.
State prominently that the source covers general material rather than DPRK-specific material.

statements: New Zealand Government Procurement identifies ICT goods and services, sensitive data and business-critical functions as national-security-sensitive procurement. It directs agencies to assess suppliers, systems and supply chains; perform regular due diligence; monitor ownership and behavior changes; use security, audit and change-of-control clauses; and document evidence before excluding a supplier on national-security grounds.
limitations: The public-sector procurement guidance does not mention DPRK IT workers and must not be represented as a DPRK-specific advisory or incident response.
Legal-status precision: General procurement guidance, not an allegation or finding against a supplier and not a nationality-based exclusion rule.
State prominently that the source is not DPRK-specific.
Apply documented supplier risk and proportional controls; never exclude based solely on nationality, language, location or remote-work status.
Do not publish supplier or personnel data gathered during due diligence.
Guidance, sanctions, procurement, and coordination material is context—not evidence of a named incident or adjudicated violation.
No single nationality, language, accent, location, camera behavior, remote-work preference, technical tool, or other weak signal establishes fraud or DPRK attribution.
No people, personas, accounts, entities, images, identifiers, victim or private data, payment data, wallets, or raw indicators are retained.
